title: Infinity-Wasserstein Distributionally Robust Principal Component Analysis: Exact Reformulation, Finite-Sample Guarantee, and Efficient Algorithm
abstract: arXiv:2611.23877v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Principal component analysis (PCA) is a fundamental and ubiquitous technique for dimension reduction and representation learning, yet its empirical formulation remains vulnerable to distributional uncertainty. While distributionally robust optimization (DRO) offers a natural remedy, existing order-2 Wasserstein models of PCA either preserve the nominal PCA subspace or lack an exact reformulation. This paper demonstrates how the infinity-Wasserstein distance can reconcile these two desirable properties. For the resulting DRO model of PCA, we derive an exact finite-dimensional reformulation and explicitly identify a worst-case distribution attaining the inner maximum. Crucially, the reformulated objective retains samplewise residual information beyond the empirical covariance matrix, revealing a mechanism through which distributional robustness can reshape the learned principal subspace. translated_title: 无穷范数-Wasserstein 分布鲁棒主成分分析：精确重构、有限样本保证与高效算法
translated_abstract: 主成分分析（PCA）是一种基础且广泛使用的降维与表示学习技术，然而其经验公式仍然容易受到分布不确定性的影响。尽管分布鲁棒优化（DRO）提供了一种自然的补救途径，但现有的基于二阶 Wasserstein 距离的 PCA 鲁棒模型要么保留了名义 PCA 子空间，要么缺乏精确的重构形式。本文展示了无穷范数-Wasserstein 距离如何能够同时兼顾这两个理想的性质。对于由此得到的 PCA 分布鲁棒优化模型，我们推导出了精确的有限维重构形式，并显式地识别出达到内层最大值的最坏情况分布。至关重要的是，重构后的目标函数在经验协方差矩阵之外还保留了逐样本的残差信息，揭示了一种分布鲁棒性借此重塑所学主子空间的机制。在真实分布满足温和假设的条件下……（原文摘要在此处被截断）
tldr: 该论文提出基于无穷范数-Wasserstein 距离的分布鲁棒 PCA 模型，实现了精确的有限维重构、最坏情况分布的显式刻画、有限样本理论保证与高效算法，并揭示其目标函数通过保留经验协方差之外的逐样本残差信息，使分布鲁棒性能够重塑所学的主子空间。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes an infinity-Wasserstein distributionally robust PCA model that achieves an exact finite-dimensional reformulation, an explicitly identified worst-case distribution, finite-sample guarantees, and an efficient algorithm, revealing that its objective retains samplewise residual information beyond the empirical covariance matrix, thereby allowing distributional robustness to reshape the learned principal subspace.
